analysis.malware_family: Unknown (likely packed downloader/trojan; Delphi with NsPack + VMProtect)
analysis.executive_summary: A Windows PE32 executable named Gnil.exe (75 KB) was dynamically analyzed. The sample shows signs of packing/obfuscation (NsPack + VMProtect) and exhibits multiple suspicious capabilities, including dynamic library/function resolution (LoadLibraryA/GetProcAddress), process memory manipulation (VirtualProtect/VirtualAlloc/VirtualFree), and direct network activity (InternetGetConnectedState, URLDownloadToFileA). Registry and service functions suggest the possibility of persistence or system configuration changes. No signatures were detected by ClamAV or YARA, indicating the malware likely evades static signature-based defenses. An overlay with a 5-byte self-extracted blob was observed, likely containing encrypted configuration or a staging payload.
key_findings: Imports indicate dynamic loading, memory manipulation, and network file downloads (URLDownloadToFileA), consistent with downloader behavior.
High entropy sections and NsPack/VMProtect packers suggest obfuscation and potential payload staging (overlay extraction observed).
Registry and service-related imports (RegQueryValueExA, RegSetValueExA, OpenServiceA) imply persistence or system modification capabilities.
immediate_actions: Quarantine the file Gnil.exe; block execution in endpoints and update endpoint protection rules.
Hunt for similar PE32 executables and process memory injections on hosts; perform deep IOC hashing (MD5, imphash e4b9ed18e19490e6ddd01f2fcee8f86a).
Review DNS/HTTP traffic for recent downloads (URLMon-based); inspect network egress to identify and block command-and-control/second-stage hosts.

file_characteristics.type: PE32 executable (GUI) Intel 80386, for MS Windows

suspicious_characteristics: High entropy sections indicating packed/encrypted content

mitre_attck_mapping.evidence: Enumerates running processes including System, smss.exe, csrss.exe, wininit.exe, services.exe, lsass.exe, svchost.exe variants, and many other system processes. Shows targeted process interest with 700+ API calls monitoring process enumeration.

Multiple packer signatures detected including NsPack and VMProtect packers with unknown PE section names (.nsp0, .nsp1, .nsp2, .vmp0). High entropy sections (7.91, 7.31) indicating encrypted/compressed payload.
Binary contains overlay (5 bytes), anomalous PE characteristics with entrypoint outside mapped sections, and multiple packer indicators suggesting code obfuscation and packing.
Terminates remote process (spoclsv.exe, PID 6540) to remove evidence or security software processes.
Creates RWX (Read-Write-Execute) memory regions indicating process injection capabilities. YARA detection shows shellcode patterns ('E8 00 00 00 00 58') in process memory.
Memory injection behavior combined with process enumeration targeting lsass.exe and other privileged processes may indicate privilege escalation attempts.
Binary reads its own image data (offset 0x00000000, length 0x00012605) suggesting self-modification or reflective loading capabilities.
Stealth timeout behavior checking local time and exiting too soon, suggesting anti-analysis and sandbox evasion techniques.

threat_overview.malware_family: Unknown Packed Downloader/Trojan (Delphi with NsPack + VMProtect)

technical_analysis_summary.execution_chain: PE32 executable (Gnil.exe) executes with dynamic loading of libraries (LoadLibraryA/GetProcAddress), creates memory regions (VirtualAlloc/VirtualProtect), spawns child process spoclsv.exe, performs process injection and memory manipulation, reads own image data for reflective loading, terminates processes for indicator removal, and exhibits sandbox evasion through timeout mechanisms
evasion_techniques: Process injection with RWX memory allocation

host: Self-read operations on own image (offset 0x00000000, length 0x00012605)

containment: Immediately quarantine Gnil.exe on all affected systems and prevent execution
Isolate systems showing network connections to suspicious URLs or hosting spoclsv.exe process
Block execution of any files with .nsp or .vmp section patterns
Monitor and block InternetGetConnectedState and URLDownloadToFileA API calls in endpoint protection
eradication: Remove spoclsv.exe from C:\Windows\System32\drivers\ and any related persistence mechanisms
Scan memory for RWX allocations and injected code, terminate suspicious processes
Remove registry keys or services related to persistence mechanisms identified during analysis
Clean system of any dropped or modified files beyond spoclsv.exe
Perform deep system scan using updated signatures for NsPack/VMProtect packed malware
recovery: Update endpoint protection with YARA rules targeting VMProtect/NsPack packers and shellcode patterns
Implement behavioral monitoring for process injection, dynamic library loading, and reflective code loading
Enhance network monitoring for URLDownloadToFileA downloads and unusual HTTP/HTTPS traffic
Conduct forensic review of process creation logs and registry changes from past 30 days
Educate users on avoiding execution of suspicious PE32 files from unknown sources
